concept: The story of India's reply is one partnership with two very different speeds, so the post is built as a split. The hero greys out New Zealand's 368 and puts India's 130 stand in white. Slide 2 is a two-bar speed test: Jaiswal's bar runs at 95.5 runs per 100 balls and Rahul's is less than half as long. caption:
One attacked. One waited. Together they put on 130.

New Zealand were bowled out for 368 at the Basin Reserve. India's openers then took the reply to 130 before Matt Henry had Yashasvi Jaiswal caught behind for 85.

Jaiswal made his 85 off 89 balls with 16 fours, surviving a dropped catch by Glenn Phillips. KL Rahul went the other way: 52 not out off 116 balls, keeping one end shut while Jaiswal took on the bowling.

India closed day 2 on 159 for 1. Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal (16 not out) resume 209 runs behind with nine wickets in hand.
